description: The bar chart illustrates the performance distribution across three language models—Claude3.5, GPT4o, and Doubao—based on a character-based act-adaptive reward modeling framework, as described in the paper “ChARM: Character-based Act-adaptive Reward Modeling for Advanced Role-Playing Language Agents.” The horizontal axis represents a normalized scale from 0.0 to 1.0, indicating the proportion of outcomes, while the vertical axis lists the model names. Each model’s performance is segmented into three colored components: pink for “Win” (left segment), light blue for an unlabeled middle category (possibly “Tie” or “Neutral,” as inferred from context), and light green for “Lose” (right segment). For Claude3.5, the distribution is 32.0% Win, 44.0% middle, and 24.0% Lose. GPT4o shows a stronger Win performance at 56.0%, with 18.0% middle and 26.0% Lose. Doubao falls in between with 42.0% Win, 36.0% middle, and 22.0% Lose. The legend at the bottom clarifies the color coding, though the middle category lacks a label in the legend, suggesting it may be an implicit or neutral outcome. The chart visually emphasizes GPT4o’s dominance in the “Win” category, while Claude3.5 has the highest proportion in the middle category. All bars sum to 100%, indicating a complete partition of outcomes per model.
